studios.title: Studio Skill
studios.purpose: Turn one open idea into one useful delivery.
studios.audience: Agents and people starting a Studio
studios.product: An executable Studio guide with a creation checklist and worked example.
steps: Name one product, its reader, and where it will be used.
Use the lowest Block, Job or Task that needs its delivery. Keep sNN beside the work.
Keep the main Draw, open choices, and a structured mind map. Preserve previous sketches.
Link the Jobs and Tasks that make the delivery. Keep working results with their owner.
Review the product with a person. Build the clean version, its deck, and its destination mapping.
checks: The For line names one product and one reader.
The main Draw shows alternatives and a delivery destination.
Working results and delivery files have separate homes.
Acceptance is recorded by a person, never inferred from a build.
studios.example: A reusable Studio that defines one interactive mind map page.
studios.open: Should creating a Studio require a delivery destination immediately?

studios.title: Studio Page
studios.purpose: Find a Studio, explore its design, and open its delivery.
studios.audience: People working within a Block, Job or Task
studios.product: A Studio browser with a dedicated detail page and large Draw viewer.
steps: Open the Draw and the product it proposes.
Read its delivery contract and open questions.
Open the source Studio in the workbench.
checks: Every row identifies its Studio and intended delivery.
Draw and delivery open from the same row.
The detail page keeps the reader oriented.
Narrow screens retain readable actions.
studios.example: This Block presents its seven Studios, with direct delivery and Draw links.
studios.open: Should a Studio detail open on its Draw or its delivery preview?

studios.title: Mind Map Skill
studios.purpose: Keep a readable argument connected to its drawings and slides.
studios.audience: Agents authoring and maintaining shared structure maps
studios.product: A mind map authoring guide with node rules, safe update rules, and a worked map.
steps: Name the total workflow and the question it answers.
Give each first-level branch a meaningful section and connect the argument.
Give each leaf one clear point and a stable identity.
One leaf owns one drawing; that drawing can hold several slides.
Preserve human edits, maintain node identity, and check linked files.
checks: The root explains the total workflow.
Each branch has a distinct role in the argument.
Every linked drawing resolves to a real file.
Refreshing a map preserves human additions.
studios.example: Choose a delivery → explore its form → review a working preview.
studios.open: Does an empty leaf need a drawing immediately or when someone opens it?

studios.title: Delivery Gallery
studios.purpose: Choose a delivery by looking at a real example.
studios.audience: People and agents deciding what to hand over
studios.product: A searchable gallery page generated from curated example configuration.
steps: Filter by Skill, Page or Drawing.
See the real preview, intended reader, and files.
Open the usable example or its original material.
Export the example configuration and adapt it.
checks: Each example points to existing material.
Search and filters produce readable results and an empty state.
The preview identifies a prototype honestly.
The source configuration rebuilds the same page.
studios.example: Compare a Studio guide, an interactive map, and an editable main Draw.
studios.open: Should file formats be filters or attributes of a single delivery?

studios.title: Studio Gallery
studios.purpose: Choose how to organize a Studio by studying real examples.
studios.audience: People and agents starting a similar design
studios.product: A searchable Studio gallery with main Draws, scope, and delivery links.
steps: Browse Skill and Page design examples.
Read the purpose and delivery contract.
Open its main Draw and unresolved choice.
Open the associated product and reusable configuration.
checks: Every example names a real source Studio.
Draw and delivery links resolve.
The purpose and intended reader are visible.
The gallery does not use itself as an example.
studios.example: Study Studio Skill, Studio Page, Mind Map Skill, Mind Map Page and Delivery Skill.
studios.open: Should discovery start with a delivery type or a work scenario?

studios.title: Mind Map Page
studios.purpose: Explore an argument and edit its structure where you read it.
studios.audience: People thinking with a structured map
studios.product: An interactive map page with node editing, drawing previews, and configuration export.
steps: Move from the workflow to sections and leaves.
Rename a node, add a child, or remove a leaf.
Open the drawing attached to a leaf.
Save in this browser or export the map configuration.
checks: Rename and add-child operations appear immediately.
Saved edits survive a reload in the same browser.
Exported configuration can be imported back.
Drawing links open real previews.
studios.example: A delivery design workflow with linked Studio and Gallery drawings.
studios.open: Should editing a map create a new review round automatically?

studios.title: Delivery Skill
studios.purpose: Turn reviewed working material into a versioned, usable delivery.
studios.audience: Agents building and handing over reviewed outcomes
studios.product: A delivery guide with destination rules, version rules, and a handover checklist.
steps: Name the Studio or work level that owns the product.
Choose the reviewed material. Keep experiments in result.
Generate the product, its preview and explanation deck. Never hand-edit generated output.
Map each piece to its intended use; render text or use the owning code builder.
Open the real product, verify links and versions, and let a person mark acceptance or sending.
checks: Every delivery names a source and destination.
An existing sent version is preserved.
The generated output opens and works.
A successful build is not recorded as a human acceptance.
studios.example: A Gallery specification builds a webpage, its example configuration, main Draw and deck.
studios.open: How should a page show the difference between built, accepted, and sent?
